behaviors.behavior: A dirty tracked .shipwright/triage.jsonl no longer blocks ensure_current's merge
The absorbed content is committed, not discarded, and both sides of a genuine divergence survive the churn-resolved merge
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb.py::test_ensure_current_absorbs_dirty_triage_log_before_merging PASSED - asserts trg-main and trg-worktree both present in the merged file

behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb.py::test_ensure_current_clean_triage_log_adds_no_absorb_step PASSED - seeds a real committed log, not merely an absent one

behaviors.behavior: cross_component integration: the absorb step composes correctly with the REAL git merge + REAL churn resolver, not a mocked one
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb.py::test_ensure_current_absorbs_dirty_triage_log_before_merging PASSED - real git_origin_repo/make_worktree fixtures, no mocking of integrate_main/churn_merge

behaviors.behavior: An absorb commit that is the ONLY commit that lands (the underlying merge is a genuine no-op) is still reported integrated=True, so the caller re-pushes and the content is not lost

behaviors.behavior: A dirty triage.jsonl while a merge is already wedged (MERGE_HEAD standing) is left untouched, not staged into a possibly-unmerged index
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb.py::test_absorb_skips_when_a_merge_is_already_in_progress PASSED - regression for a Stage-2-caught unconditional-git-add bug

behaviors.behavior: The pre-existing ensure_current regression tests (noop-when-current, integrates-when-behind, blocks-on-source-conflict, CLI, lost-ledger-exit-9) are unaffected

The absorb fires on the ALREADY-CURRENT path too (not only 'behind, about to merge'), so background writes accumulating between the delivery ladder's repeat refresh calls are not silently lost at worktree teardown
The op-in-progress guard covers merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect (reusing lib.main_tree_guards.op_in_progress, fail-closed), not just a bare MERGE_HEAD check
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb.py::test_absorb_skips_when_a_merge_is_already_in_progress PASSED, plus shared/tests/test_reconcile_triage_guards.py 10/10 PASSED covering the primitive itself

behaviors.behavior: An untracked triage.jsonl is not silently promoted to tracked by this guard
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb_guards.py::test_absorb_skips_an_untracked_triage_log PASSED - asserts the ?? state directly and that nothing was staged

behaviors.behavior: Malformed/torn content is never committed by the absorb (validated via lib.triage_validate.validate_triage_text before staging)
A failed commit resets the index, leaving it exactly as it was before the call rather than staged-and-uncommitted
behaviors.evidence: shared/tests/test_ensure_current_triage_absorb_guards.py::test_absorb_resets_the_index_when_the_commit_fails PASSED - asserts the unstage AND that the producer's content survives in the worktree

behaviors.behavior: A failed add leaves the index untouched and git's stderr reaches the operator
A deletion of the append-only log is never absorbed (the guard would otherwise propagate it to main)
An unreadable log declines rather than staging bytes nothing validated
A best-effort diagnostic that itself fails never propagates out of the merge guard
